boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along University Avenue and nearby Flint corridors, each paired with one documented reason to go.

cards.title: Hands-On Exhibits for Young Visitors
cards.subtitle: University Avenue — rotating educational exhibits
cards.notes: Follow University Avenue to explore over 40 hands-on exhibits; this stop is designed primarily for children ages 2–10.
cards.short_summary: A family-oriented museum with changing play-and-learning exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum at 1602 W. University Avenue offers more than 40 hands-on educational exhibits, with exhibits changing monthly.
cards.access_notes: Public museum; check the museum’s current calendar and admission details before visiting.

cards.title: Enter by the Flint River Trail
cards.subtitle: University Avenue — stadium access from the trail
cards.notes: Approach the University Avenue stadium on foot or bicycle via the Flint River Trail, then use the lower-level ticket gate.
cards.short_summary: A river-trail approach to Kettering’s historic stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Atwood Stadium is at 701 University Avenue, and its policy page says walkers and bicyclists may reach the lower-level ticket gate from the Flint River Trail.
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on the scheduled event and its ticketing; follow posted stadium rules.

cards.title: Research Flint’s Automotive Archive
cards.subtitle: Water Street — Kettering’s public automotive archive
cards.notes: Continue to Water Street and reserve an archive visit to examine documents, photographs, and artifacts tied to Flint manufacturing.
cards.short_summary: Kettering’s automotive archive inside a restored carriage factory.
cards.evidence_claim: Factory One at 303 W. Water Street houses Kettering University’s automotive archive of about 100,000 documents, photographs, and artifacts; public research and tours require reservations.
cards.access_notes: The archive is available to the public by reservation; contact archives@kettering.edu or 810-762-9690.

cards.title: Browse a Year-Round Public Market
cards.subtitle: First Street — indoor vendors and market events
cards.notes: Turn onto East First Street on Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday to browse produce, prepared foods, gifts, and scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A year-round public market operating three days each week.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flint Farmers' Market is at 300 E. First Street, operates year-round, and lists produce, food, gift vendors, events, and demonstration kitchens.
cards.access_notes: The market lists Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; purchases are optional.

cards.title: See What’s Playing at the Capitol
cards.subtitle: Second Street — performances in a historic theater
cards.notes: Walk East Second Street to the Capitol Theatre and consult FIM’s event listings before choosing a film, concert, or stage performance.
cards.short_summary: A downtown performance venue with an active FIM box office.
cards.evidence_claim: Flint Institute of Music lists the Capitol Theatre at 140 E. Second Street and provides ticket-center contact information and box-office hours.
cards.source_title: Contact Info - Flint Institute of Music
cards.access_notes: Access is tied to performances and box-office operations; confirm the event schedule and ticket requirements.

cards.title: Drop Into a Free Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Second Street — contemporary gallery near Saginaw Street
cards.notes: Pause on West Second Street for the current exhibition; verify installation closures and ArtWalk timing on the gallery’s visit page.
cards.short_summary: A ground-level contemporary gallery with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Buckham Gallery is at 121 W. Second Street, presents gallery exhibitions, and states that admission is always free for everyone.
cards.access_notes: Ground-level, ADA-compliant gallery; check the visit page for current hours and exhibition-installation closures.

cards.title: View Art of the African Diaspora
cards.subtitle: Saginaw Street — the Mott-Warsh Collection downtown
cards.notes: Head south on Saginaw Street to view rotating selections from a collection centered on artists of the African diaspora.
cards.short_summary: The downtown home of the publicly shared Mott-Warsh Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: MW Gallery is the permanent downtown home of the Mott-Warsh Collection and features work by artists of the African diaspora and artists reflecting on it.
cards.access_notes: Check the gallery’s official site for the current exhibition and public visiting arrangements.

cards.title: Check the Community Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saginaw Street — exhibitions at the arts council
cards.notes: Continue along South Saginaw Street and check the council’s current program before entering its community exhibition space.
cards.short_summary: A downtown arts organization with a gallery and changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greater Flint Arts Council operates a gallery at 816 S. Saginaw Street and accepts artists for exhibitions there.
cards.source_title: Greater Flint Arts Council Summer 2024 Newsletter
cards.access_notes: Gallery access varies with exhibitions and programs; consult the council’s current calendar before departure.

cards.title: Settle In for an Evening Study Session
cards.subtitle: Kearsley Street — library resources and evening hours
cards.notes: Take East Kearsley Street to read, research, or work; Tuesday through Thursday hours extend into the evening.
cards.short_summary: Flint’s main public library and a practical off-campus study stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Gloria Coles Flint Public Library is at 1026 E. Kearsley Street and describes its mission as Flint’s place for lifelong learning.
cards.access_notes: The library lists 11 a.m.–8 p.m. Tuesday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–6 p.m. Friday–Saturday; closed Sunday–Monday.

cards.title: Search the Collection Before You Go
cards.subtitle: Kearsley Street — museum galleries and searchable art
cards.notes: Continue east on Kearsley Street, preview objects in the online collection, then use the museum address to plan an in-person visit.
cards.short_summary: An art museum whose collection can be previewed online by object and artist.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flint Institute of Arts provides an online object-and-artist collection search, and its official contact page places the museum at 1120 E. Kearsley Street.
cards.source_title: Advanced Search Objects – Flint Institute of Arts
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s official visitor information for current gallery hours, admission, and temporary closures.
